approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local genetic search over molecular graphs with a Bayesian screening layer in front of the oracle, plus one scheduling rule it added to that layer. It keeps every molecule scored in the current task, breeds from the best of them by drawing parents from high-scoring score quantiles, and builds each candidate either by connected-fragment crossover between two scored molecules, optionally finished with one mutation, or by a short chain of random atom and bond edits. Direct aromatic carbon-nitrogen exchange is switched off, a sulfur rule refuses any offspring that introduces an unusual sulfur environment its own scored parents did not already carry, candidates must pass a stable canonical identity check and both duplicate scopes, and the population greedily retains the best sixty-four molecules seen. For each announced batch of ten evaluations it breeds a fresh field of de novo offspring, fits a Gaussian process to the accepted scores of this task alone with a Tanimoto-style covariance over integer Morgan environment counts, draws ten correlated samples of the fitted function over that whole field and emits the sampled maxima one at a time with the already chosen members masked out. The scheduling rule it added is that the field is normally 160 candidates, but while the search has failed to set a new session best for three announced batches in a row it is 640. That wider state is fragile by construction: the counter is reset by any improving batch whatever its size, so the wide field is withdrawn the moment one evaluation beats the incumbent, even by a hundred-thousandth of a score unit, and must be re-earned by three further unproductive batches. In practice the wide state covers about a fifth of the run and almost never reaches the hardest, most score-compressed task.
approach.novelty: This Child changes when the regime ends, and nothing else. It adds a second counter that only runs while the regime is active: how many announced batches in a row have improved the session best. The wide field is now held through every batch of the stalled episode until two consecutive improving batches have happened, and only then does the inherited narrow field return, with both counters cleared. One improving batch is treated as what the Parent's own receipts show it usually is - a single lucky evaluation that the next batch fails to follow - rather than as proof that the search has recovered. The mechanism is borrowed from trust-region Bayesian optimization, where a sharpened state is left only after a run of measured successes, never after one; the Parent implements that literature's failure counter but not its success counter, which is exactly the asymmetry this node removes. Every earlier node of this lineage that used this trigger changed what happens inside the regime - how much the allocator trusts uncertainty, which candidates stay eligible, how wide the fresh field is, how far a local edit walks, whether crossover is used - and every one of them kept the leave-on-first-improvement exit, so none of them has tested the regime's duration. The two measured alternatives that did raise breadth everywhere lost score, so this is deliberately not a width change: the width stays exactly where the Parent bound it and only the regime's lifetime grows, roughly doubling how much of the run the element covers. The other position of this round applies the identical exit rule to a different element on a different Parent, so the two arms share no code path beyond the trigger and each is read against its own Parent.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-25b9a57765d8 is a complete matched panel: macro mean 0.601117 with population SD 0.032030, seed macros 0.645977, 0.573248 and 0.584126, per-task three-seed means deco_hop 0.708117, drd2_docking 0.988396, median_2 0.231236, sitagliptin_mpo 0.620825 and zaleplon_mpo 0.457010, and a paired delta against the Anchor n-1744a1494180 of +0.004664 (per seed +0.002879, +0.010075, +0.001038). Its one new element ran exactly as registered: 86 of 435 announced batches ranked a 640-member fresh field, the rest kept 160, no pool was truncated and no fallback fired. The behaviour that limits it is the exit rule, not the element. Recomputed here from its own fifteen published trajectories (runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-25b9a57765d8/seed-0|1|2/trajectories/<task>.jsonl, 300 records per session; the recomputation reproduces the published 86 widened batches and 32 episodes exactly): the widened regime is dismissed by the first announced batch that raises the best-so-far by any amount at all. 27 of its 32 episodes ended that way and only 5 ran to the end of a session. Of those 27 exit-forcing improvements, 10 raised the session best by less than 0.005 and 6 by less than 0.002, the smallest by 0.000008, against a median improving-batch increment of 0.008110 over all 196 improving batches. That single improvement is not evidence that the stall has ended: 17 of the 27 exits were immediately followed by another non-improving batch, and 20 of the 27 re-reached the K=3 entry condition later in the same session, a median of 4 announced batches after the exit, so the regime has to be re-earned by three more non-improving batches of inherited 160-member breadth. The consequence is an exposure-limited mechanism: in-regime batches are 86 of 435 (19.8 percent), they improve the incumbent in 27 of 86 (0.3140) against 169 of 349 (0.4842) outside, and they hold only 0.679975 of the Parent's 5.889373 total best-so-far gain, 11.6 percent of realized gain for a fifth of the batches. The brief's target task is the most starved of the element: median_2 reaches the regime in 7 of its 87 announced batches (5, 1 and 1 by seed), because its per-batch increments are small enough that almost any batch resets the counter. The obvious repair is not more width everywhere, which is measured and adverse on this ancestry (always-on 640 at -0.016060, n-da0eeecfb462; always-on 40 at -0.062417, n-fe16bf000919), and the gated arms of this trigger span a wide band around a law-free path reference of -0.001735 (n-47993ce5d053) with +0.010577 (n-61b9b3bfb40d), -0.003338 (n-137ec411f54c), -0.009718 (n-189cd716f027) and a non-compounding joint composition at -0.005132 (n-36afb69ebdd1). What is untested on this element is how long the regime should last once entered.

adoptions.applicability: Available unchanged here because this campaign's trigger already uses the source's own batch-level success definition at its own failure threshold of three, and the Parent's receipts independently show that its single-improvement exit releases the regime on improvements as small as 0.000008 that the next batch usually fails to follow. The hysteresis is realized on how long the widened fresh-offspring field is kept rather than on a region side length, because this allocator samples a fitted posterior over a finite fresh pool of molecular graphs and has no coordinate box to grow or shrink.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Success-counter hysteresis on the exit from a failure-triggered state: the modified state persists across following batches and is released only after tau_succ consecutive successes, where a success is a batch at least one of whose evaluations improves the incumbent, with the counters reset at the state change.

deviations.adopted_setting: tau_succ = 2, the minimal hysteresis, bound once before evaluation for all tasks and seeds.
deviations.paper_setting: tau_succ = 3 is the stated default success tolerance for the single-trust-region configuration.
deviations.reason: The exposure change must stay bounded under the must-preserve constraint and the compounding generation cost: recomputed on the Parent's own fifteen sessions, tau_succ = 2 takes widened batches from 86 to about 163 of 435 while tau_succ = 3 would take them to about 192, and the smaller step keeps projected generation at about half of the already-measured always-on 640 configuration.

deviations.adopted_setting: One binary state with no growth branch: the widened state is either held or released at the Parent's bound width, and nothing is ever discarded or restarted.
deviations.paper_setting: After tau_succ consecutive successes the trust region's side length is doubled, up to a maximum, and after tau_fail failures it is halved; below a minimum the region is discarded and restarted.
deviations.reason: Width is a separate, already measured axis on this ancestry with adverse always-on results at 640 and 40, so a doubling schedule would confound the exit rule with a width sweep. A restart would discard the accepted archive the Parent's positive components depend on.

deviations.adopted_setting: The inherited fresh de novo offspring pool, its generation routes, its bound widths, the single global archive and the sequential masked arg-max selection are untouched.
deviations.paper_setting: Candidates are min{100d, 5000} scrambled Sobol points regenerated per batch inside the trust region, with coordinate-sparse perturbation, and samples are allocated across several regions by an implicit bandit.
deviations.reason: Candidate construction, pool breadth and multi-region allocation are separate mechanisms in this campaign with their own measured results; keeping them fixed is what makes the exit rule an attributable single-element change.

adoptions.implementation_change: CONFIG['posterior_selector'] gains stall_success_exit_batches = 2 beside the inherited stall_threshold_batches = 3 and stalled_pool_multiplier = 64. Evolution.suggest computes stalled = self.stall_regime_active or self.stall_streak >= threshold and latches self.stall_regime_active on entry, so every announced batch of the episode ranks 640 fresh offspring; Evolution.observe advances self.stall_success_streak on an improving batch, clears it on a non-improving one, and on reaching two releases the latch and resets self.stall_success_streak and self.stall_streak to zero, restoring the inherited 160-member target.

literature_review.conclusion: Reused from the ticket's frozen Search Policy review r40-stall-exposure-and-path-noise, whose recorded finding on the TuRBO source was re-read during planning: a failure counter triggers the modified state, a success counter governs the exit, the counters reset at the state change, and the stated default success tolerance is three. This lineage already implements the failure half at K=3 and leaves the state on a single improvement, so the one element adopted is the success-counter exit with one bound tolerance of two. The trust-region geometry, the doubling branch, Sobol candidate construction, coordinate-sparse perturbation, multi-region bandit allocation and restarts are refused, and the source's own results are not evidence for this benchmark. The dose, the exposure projection and the affordability bound come from this campaign's own receipts: 27 of the Parent's 32 episodes were ended by one improving batch, 10 of those improvements were below 0.005 and 20 of 27 exits re-reached the entry threshold in the same session, which is the internal evidence that the exit rule rather than the width is the open question, and the fixed-budget benchmark source is carried only to keep the single matched panel difference read against a law-free path reference rather than against zero.

sources.applicability: The campaign's K=3 gate already implements the failure counter but leaves its regime on the first improving batch of any size, which is the opposite of the success-counter semantics. Only the exit rule and one bound tau_succ are adopted; no trust region, geometric shrink, restart or extra oracle call enters this Candidate, and the entry threshold stays at the registered K=3.
sources.finding: Each trust region keeps counters of consecutive batches that improved or failed to improve the best solution: a batch counts as a success when at least one of its evaluations improves the incumbent. The region is halved after tau_fail consecutive failures and expanded after tau_succ consecutive successes, with both counters reset to zero at every size change, so the sharpened state persists across batches and is left only after a run of measured successes; the stated default success tolerance is tau_succ = 3 and a lower bound on the region triggers a restart.
sources.title: Scalable Global Optimization via Local Bayesian Optimization (TuRBO), Eriksson et al., NeurIPS 2019

sources.applicability: Supports reading this node's single matched panel difference as uncalibrated until a law-free reference realization at the same trigger is measured, which is why the registered falsifier compares the panel delta against that reference band rather than against zero. It supplies no score, task or setting: the budget of 300 accepted observations per task and the five frozen tasks are protocol-owned.
sources.finding: Under a fixed oracle budget most molecular optimization methods reported as state of the art did not beat their predecessors across 23 single-objective tasks and 25 algorithms, and the benchmark's stated purpose is transparent, reproducible comparison at a controlled budget rather than single-run leaderboard values.
sources.title: Sample Efficiency Matters: A Benchmark for Practical Molecular Optimization, Gao, Fu, Sun and Coley, NeurIPS 2022

hypothesis: Give the existing stall regime a success-counter exit. The entry rule is untouched: one integer counter of consecutive announced batches whose accepted members fail to raise the session best-so-far held when that batch was announced, and the regime is entered when it reaches K=3. Once entered, the regime now latches and governs every following announced batch - each of them ranks the Parent's 640-member fresh offspring field instead of 160 - until this session has produced tau_succ=2 consecutive improving announced batches, at which point the Parent's inherited 160-member behaviour is restored exactly and both the non-improving counter and the in-regime success counter reset to zero. A single improving announced batch no longer ends the regime; it only advances the success counter, and one non-improving batch sets that counter back to zero. One tau_succ is bound before evaluation: no mid-run adaptation, no per-task value, no sweep. The width stays at the Parent's bound 64 per announced member, the threshold stays at 3, both counters are read only from this session's own accepted scores, the bookkeeping consumes no random numbers and changes no other law, so every session reproduces the Parent exactly until the first announced batch the Parent would have un-widened and the two sessions that never reach K=3 reproduce it completely.

finding_summary.headline: Holding the wide stall regime doubled its exposure exactly, but the extra batches added nothing: panel -0.0047 vs Parent, median_2 lower
finding_summary.insights:
Holding the wide field longer does not scale the Parent's small gain; it erased it. The Parent's +0.0047 over the Anchor becomes +0.00001 here, and on the 13 sessions that ever stall it goes from +0.0054 to zero. Either the stall-only widening never had an effect beyond path noise, or whatever value it has sits in short bursts and is diluted when the wide state is held. Either way, more exposure of this 640-member field is not a route to a better panel, and the three-success exit, which would hold it longer still, is not worth running. The route of scaling this element by exposure should stop here.

The receipts show why holding fails. With no way out except two consecutive improvements, the hold is one-way on exactly the sessions that improve rarely, so there the rule turns into the always-on wide field that was already measured to lose. The borrowed trust-region rule has a counterweight this transplant leaves out: a region that keeps failing shrinks and eventually restarts. The extra candidates were not worse choices by the model's own measure (picks in held batches sat 1.16 pool standard deviations above the field average, as in the Parent's wide batches, 1.17), but they were not better molecules. A field four times larger, bred from the same parents on a plateau, gives more of the same. The chemistry review agrees: this node is almost indistinguishable from its Parent, and median_2's leaders remain a single architecture, a quinoline joined to a bridged bis-lactam cage that the search keeps enlarging instead of changing the aromatic partner. The median_2 session held wide for 12 batches found 2 improvements where the Parent found 6 over the same stretch.

Still open: this round's law-free path reference and the parallel arm that applies the same exit rule to a different stall-time element. Neither can turn this into a gain, because -0.0047 is below the only path-noise realization measured so far (-0.0017). They will decide whether this result counts as noise or as a real loss, and whether the exposure law fails on both elements. For median_2 the evidence now points away from candidate breadth and toward changing which parents and fragments get combined.
finding_summary.results:
The new exit rule ran exactly as designed. Across the 15 task/seed sessions, 169 of 435 announced batches screened a 640-member offspring field instead of 160, up from the Parent's 86 and close to the 163 projected; 76 of them were batches the old rule would already have released. Every one of the 13 episodes that ended did so only after two improving batches in a row, the logged counters matched an independent recount in all 435 batches, nothing changed before the first held batch, and the two deco_hop sessions that never stall reproduced the Parent molecule for molecule. The target task received the most new exposure: median_2 spent 30 of its 87 batches in the wide state, against 7 in the Parent. The extra candidates did compete: in the held batches 75 percent of the picks came from beyond the first 160 positions, which is what interchangeable candidates would give.

The payoff did not follow. The held batches were the least productive batches of the run: they raised the session best 30 percent of the time and added about 0.003 per batch, against 53 percent and 0.019 for ordinary batches. Over the whole wide state the share of batches that raised the best stayed exactly at the Parent's level (0.314 against 0.314), offspring beat their best parent less often (9.3 against 12.4 percent), and when each session's first held episode is compared with the Parent over the same batches from the same starting state, the total gain is the same (0.710 against 0.711; the Child ahead in 6 sessions, behind in 6). Requiring two improvements in a row made the wide state nearly permanent where improvements are rare: 10 of the 23 episodes were still held when the session ended, and they contain 119 of the 169 wide batches; two zaleplon sessions stayed wide from batch 4 and batch 8 to the end. Non-oracle run time rose from 41 to 57 seconds per task on average but stayed under 2 percent of the task limit.

Scores: the three-seed mean fell from 0.6011 to 0.5965, a paired change of -0.0047 (seeds -0.0144, -0.0044, +0.0049; 5 task cells up, 7 down, 3 unchanged). median_2 fell from 0.2312 to 0.2277 (seeds -0.012, -0.012, +0.013). Against the Anchor the node is flat (+0.00001 where +0.002 is required), and median_2 gains +0.0049 where +0.010 is required, with seed 1 below the Anchor. The four protected tasks all stay within their margins of the Anchor: zaleplon -0.0087 of an allowed 0.02, drd2 -0.0009, deco_hop +0.0015, sitagliptin +0.0033.

molecular.headline: Mid-size fused heteroaromatics elaborated by halogen relabelling; leaders carry N-halogen imides, nitroso groups, N-C-N aminals and bridged cages
molecular.overall_character: 4,350 optimizer proposals (870 per objective, 3 search seeds x 300 evaluations) and every one parses as a valid neutral molecule. They are mid-sized and heavily cyclic: mean 23.5-32.1 heavy atoms, MW 357-462, 2.90-4.59 rings and 2.06-3.53 aromatic rings, consistent with the digest counters (ring_closure_rate 0.949-0.975, aromatic_atom_rate 0.934-0.971, branch_rate 0.947-0.972). Elaboration is almost entirely small-substituent decoration of a fused heteroaromatic core: methyl, ethyl, propyl, methoxy, acetyl, hydroxymethyl and above all halogen (digest halogen_rate 0.80-0.98 on four objectives, 0.124 on the fifth). The halogen is placed on heteroatoms as readily as on carbon: 438 and 364 of 870 proposals on two objectives contain an N-halogen bond, 246 and 353 put a halogen directly on an aromatic ring nitrogen, 40-135 per objective carry an O-halogen bond, and not one of the 4,350 proposals contains a trifluoromethyl group. No molecule carries a formal charge and none carries specified stereochemistry (digest charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five objectives), while RDKit finds unassigned stereocentres in 143-834 proposals per objective and in 84-87 of 87 molecules in three of the five top deciles. Early search is wide (228-605 distinct Murcko scaffolds per 870 proposals) but the leaders collapse: each top decile of 87 spans only 14-47 scaffolds and on three objectives a single scaffold holds 23-28 of them. Synthetic accessibility averages 3.30-4.27 with 12-160 proposals per objective above 5. Chemically this node is almost indistinguishable from its code Parent n-25b9a57765d8: group frequencies match closely on four objectives (for example N-halogen 33 vs 33 and basic amine 724 vs 726 on one objective), two of the fifteen sessions are molecule-for-molecule identical to the Parent for all 300 evaluations, and the other thirteen first differ at evaluation 51-242. The one visible distributional shift is a drop in saturated-amine and aminal content on the lowest-scoring objective (basic amine 336 vs the Parent's 516, N-C-N aminal 48 vs 156 of 870) alongside more one- to six-atom fragments there (23 vs 12).

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals averaging 23.5 heavy atoms, MW 357, logP 3.80, TPSA 58, 2.90 rings and 2.41 aromatic rings. One family dominates: an alkyl/methoxy-substituted indole- or azaindole-2-carboxamide carrying an N-aryl (often 3-pyridyl) amide, grown from the initial molecule COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC (0.3051). In the leaders both the amide nitrogen and the ring nitrogen are halogenated rather than N-H or N-alkyl, as in CCc1c(OC)nc2c(cc(C(=O)N(F)c3ccccc3)n2F)c1C. A second family is a dihydrobenzofuran-fused cinnamamide with N-Br, CNc1cc(N)c(C=CC(=O)N(Br)c2cccc(F)c2)c2c1CC(Br)O2. 438 of 870 proposals contain an N-halogen bond and 246 a halogen on an aromatic ring nitrogen; the top decile of 87 holds 82 N-halogen molecules against only 11 with an N-H amide, and spans 14 Murcko scaffolds with 23 sharing O=C(Nc1cccnc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1.
liabilities: N-fluoro, N-chloro and N-bromo amides in 438 of 870 proposals and 82 of the 87 highest-scoring molecules
Halogen bonded to an aromatic ring nitrogen in 246 proposals, including every digest best molecule
An O-F bond on a scored leader, CNc1cc(N)c(C=CC(=O)N(Br)c2cccc(OF)c2)c2c1CCO2 at 0.3748
One- and two-atom species consuming oracle calls at the 0.0 floor, including 12 after evaluation 200 (N, Br, BrBr, FC1CCN1)
An alpha-bromo ether on the second family's leader, CNc1cc(N)c(C=CC(=O)N(Br)c2cccc(F)c2)c2c1CC(Br)O2
missing_features: An N-H or N-alkyl amide in the leading family: the top decile carries an N-halogen amide in 82 of 87 molecules and an N-H amide in only 11
A free indole or azaindole N-H donor; the best molecules cap that nitrogen with F, Cl or Br
Any basic amine centre in the leaders: 0 of 87 top-decile molecules, against 95 of 870 proposals overall
Polar solubilising handles: zero carboxylic acids and zero sulfonamides in all 870 proposals
A trifluoromethyl or other polyhalogenated carbon substituent: zero in 870 proposals

Ring-skeleton variation late in the run; after evaluation 200 the changes are terminal heteroatom labels, and 127 of 870 proposals are halogen-relabelling duplicates of a molecule already scored in the same session
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score climbs with size and aromatic ring count (top decile 25.1 heavy atoms and 2.80 aromatic rings against 10.0 and 0.78 in the bottom decile) and with an aryl amide (88.5 percent of the top decile against 17.2 percent of the bottom). Inside the leading family the score is completely flat to halogen identity: the digest lists twelve molecules at exactly 0.4828171386373609 differing only in F/Cl/Br on the two nitrogens and in ring heteroatom placement, and fifteen molecules in seed 1 sit on that same value. The 0.0 floor is occupied by one- and two-atom species. The gradient rewards a lipophilic bicyclic heteroaromatic bearing one anilide-like amide and gives no signal at all on the halogen permutations the late budget is spent on.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and most polar set: 870 proposals averaging 32.1 heavy atoms, MW 462, logP 3.60, TPSA 125, 4.24 rings and 3.53 aromatic rings. Two families lead. The first is a fused triazolo-pyrimidinone thione bearing an N-linked quinazoline and decorated with a hypofluorite and an alpha-chloro ether: O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3 (0.8561, four aromatic rings, MW 473). The second is an acetyl- and formyl-substituted indolenine carrying two nitroso groups and bonds drawn across the interior of its benzene ring, written cc2-3, which RDKit perceives as three four-membered rings: COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2. Nitroso appears in 240 of 870 proposals, nitrile in 255, thione or thiol in 206, and 85 proposals contain a ring of four or fewer atoms all of whose atoms are aromatic. Amides are nearly absent (21 of 870, 2.4 percent) and sulfonamides absent entirely. Seeds 0 and 2 reproduce the Parent molecule-for-molecule for all 300 evaluations, so only seed 1 contributes distinct chemistry here.
liabilities: A hypofluorite O-F bond plus an alpha-chloro, alpha-fluoro ether on the highest-scoring molecule of this objective
Aryl and alkyl nitroso groups in 240 of 870 proposals and 48 of the 87 leaders
Bonds drawn across the interior of a six-membered aromatic ring in 85 proposals and 20 of 87 leaders
Synthetic accessibility above 5 for 149 of 870 proposals, the worst of the five objectives
Two-atom and three-atom proposals scored at the 0.5 floor (C=C, N=O, C=C=NN=C=C, ClCOCOCl), three of them after evaluation 200
missing_features: Amide or sulfonamide linkers between the ring systems: 21 of 870 proposals contain an amide, none a sulfonamide
Ionisable or basic centres for molecules of MW 462 and TPSA 125: basic amines in only 40 of 870 proposals and 1 of 87 leaders
Ordinary ortho-fused bicyclics in place of transannular aromatic bonds, which occur in 20 of the 87 leaders
Defined stereochemistry: 424 of 870 proposals and 56 of 87 leaders carry unassigned stereocentres
Carbon-bound polyhalogen substituents in place of the O-F and alpha-chloro ether groups the leaders use: zero trifluoromethyl in 870 proposals
Hydrogen-bond donors other than inherited hydroxyls, which fall from 42 of 87 in the bottom decile to 2 of 87 in the top
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises with lipophilicity and rotatable-bond count rather than with clean fusion: top decile logP 4.56 and 8.49 rotatable bonds against 1.93 and 2.90 in the bottom decile, at nearly equal heavy-atom count (32.3 against 19.9). Three decorations track the top decile: a nitroso group (48 of 87 against 5 of 87 in the bottom decile), a nitrile (32 against 8) and an O-halogen bond (11 against 4). Topological strain is rewarded too: 20 of the 87 leaders carry an all-aromatic ring of four or fewer atoms and 51 carry a four-membered ring fused to an aromatic ring. The floor sits at exactly 0.5 and is occupied by one- and two-atom species, so the objective gives no pressure to shrink and no pressure to be makeable.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals averaging 30.3 heavy atoms, MW 452, logP 5.25, TPSA 47, 3.90 rings, 2.06 aromatic rings and fsp3 0.38, the most saturated and most lipophilic of the five sets. per_task.score_gradient_reading: The clearest gradient of the five and it is driven by one feature: a basic sp3 amine is present in all 87 top-decile molecules and in only 20 of 87 at the bottom. Score rises as polarity falls (top decile TPSA 28.6 against 82.7) and as the sulfonamide and carboxylic-acid chemistry inherited from the initial molecules disappears: the bottom decile is 41 of 87 sulfonyl-amide and 28 of 87 carboxylic acid, the top decile zero of each, and the floor is literally the seed pyrrolidine sulfonamide fragment, O=C(NCl)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.000167. The objective rewards a lipophilic basic amine on a two-carbon linker between two aryl rings and the generator found that pattern; it reaches it through a hydrolytically labile aminal in 68 of the 87 leaders.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises steeply with size and ring content (top decile 27.4 heavy atoms, 4.03 rings and 2.67 aromatic rings against 11.5, 1.40 and 0.87 at the bottom) and with fluorine placement on nitrogen: 65 of the 87 leaders carry an N-halogen bond against 8 of 87 at the bottom, and 60 carry a saturated-ring amine. The worst scores, down to 7.7e-27, are single atoms (F, O, S) and two-atom species (FBr). The gradient rewards a polar fused heteroaromatic with several fluorines and a saturated amine ring, but it does not distinguish where the fluorine sits, so the generator satisfies it with N-F and O-F bonds; 133 of the 870 proposals, the highest of the five objectives, are halogen-relabelling duplicates of a molecule already scored in the same session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over 4,350 optimizer proposals read from this node's fifteen staging trajectories, two objectives contain an N-halogen bond in 438 and 364 of their 870 proposals, and 246 and 353 of those put the halogen directly on an aromatic ring nitrogen; O-halogen bonds appear in 40 to 135 proposals per objective. The pattern is not confined to weak molecules: 82 of 87 and 65 of 87 molecules in two leader deciles carry an N-halogen bond, the highest-scoring molecule on a third objective carries a hypofluorite O-F bond, and one leader set has an N-halogen amide in 82 of 87 molecules against an N-H amide in only 11.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator bonds halogen to nitrogen and oxygen as freely as to carbon, and treats the two as interchangeable edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen substitution is the operator set's cheapest edit and it is applied without regard to the element it attaches to, so the search converts hydrogen-bond donors into bleach-like N-X and O-X bonds whenever a score depends on halogen count. A task-agnostic generator would type the attachment atom in its substitution operator, keeping halogen on carbon and leaving N-H and O-H donors intact unless an explicitly requested edit forms the heteroatom bond.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one of the 4,350 proposals contains a trifluoromethyl group and none contains a trifluoromethoxy group, while the same proposal sets contain 651 to 843 carbon-bound single halogens per 870 molecules on three objectives. The fluorine-richest leader set reaches its score with N-F, O-F, fluoromethyl and fluoroethyl arms (COC1C(F)=C(F)C(F)=C1n1cc2c(c1C1C=CCNC1)c(=O)n(F)c(=N)n2F) rather than with any CF3.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build a polyhalogenated carbon substituent; it only ever adds one halogen per heavy atom.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Substituent growth is one atom at a time, so a three-fluorine carbon needs three accepted consecutive edits on the same atom and is effectively unreachable. A task-agnostic generator would carry small multi-atom substituent fragments (polyhalomethyl, polyhalomethoxy, difluoromethylene) as single atomic edits in its mutation vocabulary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest counters give charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five objectives over 870 proposals each, and structural perception of the same molecules confirms zero formal charges in 4,350 proposals. Yet unassigned stereocentres appear in 143 to 834 proposals per objective and in 84 to 87 of the 87 molecules in three leader deciles; one leader set has an undefined centre in every one of its 87 molecules, at the carbon that also carries the aryl group responsible for its score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The representation expresses neither formal charge nor configuration, so no proposal is a defined stereoisomer or an ionised species.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Every sp3 centre the operators build is an undefined mixture, and any score channel that distinguishes enantiomers, diastereomers or protonation state is being optimised against an unspecified average. A task-agnostic generator would either emit configuration explicitly on the centres it creates or restrict its ring and chain operators to edits that do not create undefined centres.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 85 and 55 proposals per 870 on two objectives contain a ring of four or fewer atoms every atom of which is aromatic, that is a bond drawn across the interior of an aromatic ring, and those motifs survive into the leaders (20 of 87 and 9 of 87). Small rings fused to an aromatic ring appear in 46 to 188 proposals per objective and in 26 to 51 of the 87 molecules of three leader deciles. On another objective 77 of 87 leaders contain a ring of eight or more atoms that shares at least two atoms with a second ring, a bridged cage, with 1.67 bridgehead atoms per molecule, and the leader sets score 4.36 to 4.70 on synthetic accessibility with 8 to 23 of 87 above 5.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-editing operators create transannular, strained and bridged ring systems with no geometric or strain feasibility check.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation, ring bridging and ring contraction are currently validated by valence and canonical identity only, so any pair of in-ring atoms is a legal bond target. A task-agnostic generator would make those operators aware of ring size, aromatic-ring interiors and bridgehead geometry, and reject bonds whose smallest resulting ring cannot be built.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective an N-C-N aminal appears in 243 of 870 proposals and in 68 of the 87 leaders, including molecules scored above 0.999 (CCCc1cccc(CCN2CCCCNC2c2ccc(F)c(Cl)c2)c1C). On another, enamine or enamide double bonds inside a bridged bis-lactam cage appear in most leaders (CCCc1cc(N2C3CC4=C(CCN4C(=O)CN(C)C3=O)C2CC)c2ccccc2n1), and alpha-halo ethers and alpha-halo aminals occur in scored leaders on three objectives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Newly formed centres are not checked for hydrolytic stability, so labile aminals and enamines become the dominant leader motif.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The admission gate accepts any valence-legal molecule, so the cheapest way to place a required pharmacophore next to a ring is through a centre that would hydrolyse before assay. A task-agnostic generator would include a post-edit stability screen for newly created acetal, aminal, alpha-halo-heteroatom and enamine centres, or finish them into their stable counterparts.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 11 to 133 proposals per objective, 1.3 to 15.3 percent, are duplicates of a molecule already scored in the same session once halogens are relabelled. One session proposed fifteen molecules at one identical score, and the digest lists twelve of them at exactly 0.4828171386373609, differing only in F, Cl or Br on two nitrogens and in ring heteroatom placement (CCc1c(OC)nc2c(cc(C(=O)N(F)c3ccccc3)n2F)c1C against CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3cccnc3)n2Br)c1C). Leader deciles collapse to 14 to 47 Murcko scaffolds out of 87, with a single scaffold holding 23 to 28 of them on three objectives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Once a family converges, the generator's only remaining edit is a terminal-atom relabelling the score cannot distinguish.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Late proposals exercise the substituent-label part of the operator set and not the skeleton, so an exhausted family keeps consuming evaluations on score-identical variants. A task-agnostic generator would detect that a candidate is equivalent to an already-scored molecule under substituent relabelling and spend that proposal on a skeleton-level edit (ring fusion change, scaffold replacement) instead.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Carboxylic acids are absent from 870 proposals on two objectives and number 1 and 4 on two more; the 51 acids and 75 sulfonyl-amides on the remaining objective are inherited from the initial molecules and vanish from its leaders (41 of 87 sulfonyl-amides and 28 of 87 acids in the bottom decile, zero of each in the top). On the objective whose gradient is driven by a basic amine, the generator did find one (87 of 87 leaders), but on another objective the leaders carry no basic amine at all (0 of 87, against 95 of 870 overall) and hydroxyl donors fall from 42 of 87 at the bottom to 2 of 87 at the top of a third.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator strips polar and ionisable handles rather than installing them, and cannot grow an acid, a sulfonamide or a ring amine de novo.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation vocabulary adds lipophilic and halogenated atoms far more often than polar functional groups, so the search drifts to high logP (one leader decile averages 5.25, individual leaders 6.81) and loses hydrogen-bond donors it started with. A task-agnostic generator would include explicit polar-group insertion edits (carboxyl, sulfonamide, basic ring nitrogen, amide N-H) at comparable proposal weight to halogen substitution.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

Disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange, stable canonical/isomeric identity admission, emitted/initial and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, max 120 atoms.

Radius-2 chirality-aware 2048-bin integer Morgan-count features, generalized dot-product Tanimoto GP fitted only to accepted labels, adaptive mean and population-SD normalization with 0.001 floor, noise SD 0.05, float64 Cholesky with the jitter ladder.
